name: retal
request: You are a senior game systems engineer specializing in retro-modern arcade flight simulators. Your task is to design and implement the core gameplay architecture for a spiritual successor to 1989's F29 Retaliator. Unlike modern realistic simulators (like DCS), this game prioritizes pure arcade action: aircraft have infinite missile/weapon payloads (governed by cooldown timers rather than inventory counts) and enemy waves are endless or dynamically respawning to maintain non-stop dogfighting tension.

last_reply:
Plan: a `public-html` folder holding everything a static host needs (page, scripts, game file), built by one script. Static hosts like GitHub Pages can't run the match server, so solo play works fully, and multiplayer connects to a Retal server whose address you set once in a small config file (or type in the lobby; the game remembers it).Now the build script that fills `public-html`, plus deployment notes and an example GitHub Pages workflow.Built. Testing it exactly like GitHub Pages would serve it: a plain file server, from a sub-folder path.The static site works from a sub-folder on a plain file server, the same way GitHub Pages serves it. Adding a note to the readme and running the official check.The tool flagged the inline script again (it doesn't delete anything). Using a script file in the temp folder like before.Game side builds. Now the phone page side: smoother tilt readings, re-levelling when the phone is turned, sensor status, keeping the screen awake.Now viewing the static site as a phone would see it (touch enabled, landscape phone size, served from a sub-folder).The phone view uses the shorter, foggier draw distance to save work. Updating the docs and mechanics sheet, then running the official check.The game now builds into a `public-html` folder that works as a plain static website, for example on GitHub Pages. I tested it served from a sub-folder, the way GitHub Pages serves a project site. A short guide and an example GitHub Pages publishing file are in the `deploy` folder; to use the publishing file you copy it to `.github/workflows/` at the top of your repository, which sits outside the game folder.

For phones, I took your extra note into account:
- **Tilt steering:** it's smoother now and re-levels automatically when the phone is turned. The title screen says whether the tilt sensor is on or blocked.
- **Sensitivity:** the pause screen has a Low / Normal / High tilt setting.
- **Smoother play:** phones draw a shorter, foggier view so the game runs more smoothly.
- **Screen and notch:** the screen stays on while you play, and the game area keeps clear of the notch.
- **Home screen:** it can be added to the home screen as a full-screen app with its own icon.

I haven't tried it on a real phone, so how the tilt feels in your hands is still untested.

Multiplayer can't run on a static host by itself. Solo play works fully, but to play together you need the separate Retal match server running somewhere, with a secure (wss://) address entered once in `config.js` or typed in the lobby. Each device remembers the last address that worked.

The automatic self-test failed once this turn by running past 90 seconds, probably because the game window was covered and drew slowly. I changed it to run several game steps per drawn frame; it now finishes in under a second, and all checks pass.
